events.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (delayed to Thu noon ET) — distillate stocks last 104.2M bbl, roughly 14% below the five-year average
events.note: Added Sep 7 night: the last supply data before Thursday's PPI, and the direct test of whether the refining constraint is easing. Crude stocks sit about 1% ABOVE their five-year average while distillate sits 14% below — the split that put the diesel crack at a record above $106/bbl against a normal $15-25. Another distillate draw extends the shortage into the print; a build is the first evidence it is easing. Updated Sep 9 morning: the release moved from Wednesday 10:30 AM to Thursday noon ET because of the September 7 federal closure, so the first supply data since the Saudi outages now lands the same morning as August PPI rather than a day ahead of it.

events.label: ECB rate decision — a 25bp increase widely expected, same day as US PPI
events.note: Added Sep 4 night: the euro area decision lands the same morning as August PPI, so two policy inputs hit the dollar and global duration at once. A hike alongside a hot US producer-price print pushes both long ends the same way.

events.label: Oracle Q1 FY2027 results, after the close — options pricing a roughly 10% move on consensus of $1.67 a share and ~$19.1B revenue
events.note: The test of the AI capex bid that held the Nasdaq's Sep 8 loss to a third of the Dow's.

events.label: August PPI (8:30 AM ET) — first of the two inflation prints Waller's hold is conditioned on
events.note: Added Sep 3 night: producer prices are where tariff and energy pass-through shows up before it reaches CPI, and they arrive two days after Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect. ISM services prices paid at 72.6 and manufacturing prices at 71.1 argue the risk is to the upside. Waller said it 'may not take much acceleration in inflation' to move him back toward tightening, so this is the first of two prints that can undo the ~12-point repricing of September 3.

events.label: August CPI (8:30 AM ET) — the last inflation print before the FOMC, four trading days out
events.note: Added Sep 3 night: the print that resolves Waller's condition with no scheduled Fed communication left to soften it. Core CPI at or under 0.3% month over month keeps the hold intact; above 0.3% re-arms the hike inside four trading days of the September 15-16 decision, and would reverse the September 3 rally on the same mechanism that produced it.

events.label: Iran-Oman temporary Hormuz transit route — date not fixed, described Sep 7 as in its final stages
events.note: Added Sep 9 morning: a signal window rather than a scheduled event — the date is indicative. Hormuz is effectively closed to commercial traffic, with roughly 6 transits on Aug 30 against about 85 a day normally. A signed route would remove the war premium from crude but not the demand leg underneath it: Chinese imports were 8.93M b/d in August, up 6.2% on July. So a settlement is not symmetrical with the escalation that produced $100 Brent.

events.label: FOMC decision (Sep 15-16) — futures pricing roughly 57% odds of a quarter-point hike to 3.75%-4.00%
events.note: The long end broke its range the week before the meeting: 10Y through 4.818% to 4.857%, 30Y at 5.30%. What the curve does if a hike is delivered is the question, not the hike.

events.label: Bank of Japan policy decision — markets pricing a September hike after Deputy Governor Himino flagged upside inflation risks
events.note: Added Sep 4 morning: the yen reached 155.28 per dollar on Sep 3, its strongest in a month, on BOJ hike bets rather than on the Fed alone. The decision lands two days after the Sep 15-16 FOMC, so the funding currency behind a large share of global duration positioning reprices twice inside four sessions. A yen driven by Japanese tightening keeps appreciating on a hot US print as well as a soft one; USD/JPY back above 158 would say the BOJ leg was overstated.

events.label: US import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcoholic beverages take effect
events.note: Follows Canada's 15%-50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods (Sept 8) and the removal of Canadian-origin products from federal schedules worth $50B+ a year. A cost-push input running alongside $100 crude.

events.label: Treasury expanded long-end buyback program ends — ops of at least $4B run from September 9
events.note: The count of completed operations is what separates absorbed supply from purchased calm at the long end. 30Y at 5.30%, with 5.33% the August 18 nineteen-year high above it.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
